minor.issue: The backend accepts an email change for ANY signed-in account, including password/email accounts, with only a code to the new email. There's no current-password or old-email confirmation. The UI only offers it when there's no email, but someone holding a session could swap the account email through the API and then use password reset. Restrict it to accounts without an email, or require re-auth.

'Change' replaces an existing phone sign-in method without re-auth, and nothing is sent to the account email. A hijacked session can add a persistent phone login. Consider asking for the password (or the old phone) and sending a security notice email.

critical_code_review_comments: spenza.js tick(): the link query uses 'spenzaUser.linkedAt': null. For real (non-dry) lines, buy()/buyMobile() store spenzaUser without linkedAt, so tick will call /sims/{iccid}/assign once each line is active. That's intended. Note that buy() records spenzaUser before activation, while syncUser only touches lines with an iccid, so a line still provisioning when the email changes is fixed later by linkUser's email-mismatch check, but only if tick re-selects it. It won't: linkedAt is set once and tick only picks lines without linkedAt. Activation happens after the buy, though, so tick links it with the current email. Fine in practice.

linkUser in syncUser runs sequentially with no Spenza-side error marker (userLinkFailedAt is set only by tick). A failed /assign during an email change leaves the line on the old private email with linkedAt set, so tick never retries it. Consider clearing linkedAt or setting userLinkFailedAt on syncUser failures.

spenzaUser() sends phoneNumber with only the +1 prefix stripped. A non-US phone (e.g. +44…) is sent as a full international digit string, which Spenza may reject in user{}. Consider sending it only for +1 numbers.

remind(): the topup URL uses Math.max(5, ceil(short)), but the wallet minimum shown in the UI is $10 ('Amount (USD, min $10)'). A short of $1–9 prefills an amount below the minimum. Consider Math.max(10, …).
